issue.title: TUI app import loads 3292 modules against the 3290 cap (test_app_import_budget)
issue.description:
# CI failure: TUI app import loads 3292 modules against the 3290 cap

## CI failure

- **Node:** `tests/ace/tui/test_app_import_budget.py::test_tui_app_import_stays_under_startup_budget`

Deterministic module-count overrun, not the timing flake. The assertion is `assert 3292 < 3290`:
importing the TUI app loads 3292 modules against the 3290 cap. Reproduced 2026-09-20 in workspace
sase_32 at master `244442ee8` in the full lane, in isolation (twice), and with the working tree's
`src/` changes reverted to `HEAD`.

Distinct from sase-136 (closed 2026-09-19): that fixed wall-clock flakiness by measuring CPU time
and explicitly says "do not raise the CPU budget or module cap". This is the cap itself being
exceeded by two modules, so recent import-graph growth is the suspect; which commit added them is
NOT established. Caveat to rule out first: this workspace's venv also has the required plugins
installed (`setup_required_plugins`), so confirm the count is not plugin-dependent before
bisecting. Fix by removing the new eager imports, not by raising the cap.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Deterministic module-count overrun (assert 3292 < 3290), not a timing flake: fails in the full lane, twice in isolation, and with the working tree's src reverted to HEAD. sase-136 already made the timing CPU-based.

payload.description: sase-136 fixed the wall-clock flake in this same test and kept the 3290-module cap; this is that cap now being exceeded by 2 modules, a different root cause

payload.entry: ROOT CAUSE AND FIX (found by the sase-11y.7 gate repair, 2026-09-20, workspace sase_32): the overrun is attributable, not unattributed or environment-shaped. Importing sase.ace.tui.app in a clean interpreter loads 3285 modules at eaa1cbf4d (before the Services-tab phase; passes the 3290 cap), 3292 at 244442ee8 and at 6087c0a8e. Six of the added modules are sase.service.{status,boot,config,paths,state,control}, pulled by two eager import edges that the sase-11y.7 phase added: src/sase/ace/tui/actions/axe_display/_data.py (c2befdbb3, module-level imports of sase.service.control/paths/status) and src/sase/ace/tui/widgets/bgcmd_list.py (92dd554c4, sase.service.status imported for a runtime isinstance check). The sase-11y.7 gate-repair change defers both (TYPE_CHECKING plus function-local imports inside the service-host-enabled branch; duck-typed enablement check) and does NOT raise the cap: the count is now 3286 and only sase.service and sase.service.restart are loaded. tests/ace/tui/test_app_import_budget.py now also asserts sase.service.status and sase.service.control are absent after the import, so a future eager edge fails with a named module. The change sits in that worktree pending its host-owned commit; once it lands this bead can be closed on evidence. One further module of the 3285 to 3292 growth is not attributed here; 3286 is 4 under the cap.

DUPLICATE MERGED IN + STATE CHANGED (2026-09-20 triage, athena workspace sase_34, master ec7dbbfdf == origin/master).

Duplicate: sase-13r (filed 4m51s later, athena workspace sase_31) is closed as superseded by this bead. Its unique evidence, carried forward: the count was exactly 3292 on every run and at each of 244442ee8, 9cfb06a54, 9231c9352, 65c8169f9 and e65cc22ee replayed in detached worktrees; and a change that added 3 non-TUI modules (service/effective_env.py, lease retryability imports) left the count at exactly 3292 before and after, proving those modules are outside the TUI import chain. It also held 3 independent corroborations.

THE NUMBERS IN THIS BEAD ARE NOW STALE -- the fix landed halfway. The two eager import edges named in the ROOT CAUSE note are gone: src/sase/ace/tui/actions/axe_display/_data.py no longer imports sase.service.* at module level, and src/sase/ace/tui/widgets/bgcmd_list.py now imports ServiceEnablement/ServiceStatusProc under TYPE_CHECKING only (line 24). tests/ace/tui/test_app_import_budget.py also grew a deferred_modules assertion that pins sase.service.status and sase.service.control as deferred, and that assertion passes.

What remains is a boundary saturation, not an overrun: the node now fails 'assert 3290 < 3290'. _MAX_MODULE_COUNT is 3290 (tests/ace/tui/test_app_import_budget.py:12) and the comparison is strict less-than, so importing sase.ace.tui.app at exactly the cap is red. The residual work is therefore much smaller than this bead's 'large' size suggests and the direction is a deliberate choice between two options: cut at least one more module from the TUI startup import closure so the count lands strictly under the cap, or change the guard's boundary semantics to <= with a recorded rationale for why exactly-at-cap is acceptable. Both remain consistent with closed sase-136's instruction not to raise the cap. Whoever fixes this must re-measure first, since the reported 3292 no longer reproduces.

evidence.note: Independent repro 2026-09-20: fails deterministically in isolation (-n0) on a pristine export of origin/master ec7dbbfdf and on ec7dbbfdf+sase-11y.10.1.2, with 'assert 3290 < 3290' (the module count is now exactly at the cap; the strict < fails). Not load-related, so not the sase-136 timing flake.

Reproduced deterministically on master d9ae431dc during the sase-11y.10.1.7 landing. That tree first failed the test's deferred_modules assertion (sase.service.status/control pulled in via sase.main.update_types -> sase.service.actions, a regression from d65316234 / sase-11y.10.1.3.1.3), at 3297 modules. The landing made that import TYPE_CHECKING-only, which clears deferred_modules and drops the count to 3290, still failing 'assert 3290 < 3290'. The remaining overage is this bead's budget creep and is unrelated to the service-host work (the only other sase.service module left, sase.service.restart, arrives via sase.supervision.restart and dates to 13ea3da51 on 2026-09-17).
